anya: Heads-up — saw memory creep on a long-context load test. Heap went up ~200MB over 20k tokens and never dropped. Repro on master and on 2026-03-14-nightly. :worried:

sam: Oof. Any stack or perf traces?

anya: Attached perf log (snippet):
```
KVCache::alloc_page  id=42 size=1MB ts=1815006700
append_block offset=98304 len=512 tag=request-abc
evict_page id=17 freed=0 (refcount!=0)
alloc_page id=43 size=1MB ts=1815006745
append_block offset=98304 len=256 tag=request-def
```
Looks like append offset reuses 98304 across requests.

maria: That offset repeats... could be wrong token alignment rounding when computing page slot? We switched to 4k-aligned pages in that PR.

liam: I remember a change in page coalescing where small fragments get packed into 96KB slots. If the slot rotation logic doesn't reset request tag, cross-request blocks might be read as live.

anya: I tried a minimal repro: two sequential requests A then B with long contexts. After B completes, A's tail appears in B's response cache hits (intermittent). Steps: 1) start server with --kv-debug 2) send req A with 15k tokens 3) send req B with 2k tokens 4) observe cache hits in B for tags from A.

sam: Can you paste the debug lines for the contamination?

anya: Sure:
```
[1815006761] KVPage read id=42 slot=12 tag=request-A seq=14987
[1815006761] KVPage read id=42 slot=12 tag=request-B seq=28
[1815006761] KVBlock stale_tag_mismatch slot=12 found_tag=request-A expected=request-B
```

liam: That stale_tag_mismatch is the smoking gun. I suspect the migration path that copies leftover fragments during eviction forgot to clear the tag field when moving fragments between slots.

maria: Also saw perf regression: throughput drops 5% when eviction hot-loop hits this branch due to extra checks. Profile shows ~3% CPU in kv::check_tag in hot path.

sam: Could be two bugs: (1) tag clearing on free/move and (2) alignment math returning the same slot for different logical offsets if offset%slot_size rounding uses floor instead of div.

anya: I pushed a quick instrumented build with additional assertions. bench-bot ran long-context nightly and flagged 3 failures. I put logs in /tmp/kv-leak-logs.tar.gz.

bench-bot: nightly-run: long-context-20k: 3 assertions failed, avg mem growth 180MB, flakiness 0.6%

liam: Proposed fix idea (pseudo):
```
// when evicting/moving a fragment
memcpy(dest, src, len);
// ensure tag and seq fields are reset for dest
dest->tag = CURRENT_REQUEST_NONE;
dest->seq = 0;
```
Also add atomic fence around slot rotation to avoid ABA when concurrent allocs wrap.

maria: Nice. We should also add a debug-mode sanitizer to assert tag==CURRENT_REQUEST_NONE on free. That'll catch stale blocks earlier.

sam: Can someone craft a tiny unit test that simulates slot wrap? I can land tests once patch exists. We need to cover: free->alloc race, move copy preserves tag, and alignment math for slot index.

anya: I'll write the reproducer and a small C++ test harness that drives the allocator with explicit offsets to force wrap. Will push branch ny/kv-slot-reset.

liam: Quick perf note — if we always zero tag on free, that's cheap (8 bytes). The costly part was an extra conditional we added earlier for the fragmentation coalescer; avoid branching in hot path. Use unconditional store instead.

sam: Cool. @deploy-bot can we get a canary with ny/kv-slot-reset after tests pass?

deploy-bot: Canary pipeline queued: canary-1815-kv-reset. No blocking tests. ETA ~18m.

anya: After that we should run the long-context nightly again. If mem growth is gone and stale_tag logs vanish, ship patch.

maria: Also open a follow-up to audit all places that copy/move blocks — we probably missed a couple of edge codepaths (rollback, snapshot restore).

liam: Agreed. I'll do a quick grep for memcpy(...kv_block...) and review.

sam: Thanks team. Keep thread updated. If someone finds an urgent repro that shows cross-request data in outputs (not just logs), tag #incidents.

anya: Will post branch and test results here when ready. :thumbsup:
